passages.quote: A control system is a system of integrated elements whose function is to maintain a process variable at a desired value or within a desired range of values.
Automatic control systems neither replace nor relieve the operator of the responsibility for maintaining the facility.
Control system input is the stimulus applied to a control system from an external source to produce a specified response from the control system.
Control system output is the actual response obtained from a control system.
An open-loop control system is one in which the control action is independent of the output.
A closed-loop control system is one in which control action is dependent on the output.
Feedback is information in a closed-loop control system about the condition of a process variable.
A controlled variable is the process variable that is maintained at a specified value or within a specified range.
A manipulated variable is the process variable that is acted on by the control system to maintain the controlled variable at the specified value or within the specified range.
An automatic control system is a preset closed-loop control system that requires no operator action.
the four basic functions that occur are:
The three functional elements needed to perform the functions of an automatic control system are:
The measuring element performs the measuring function by sensing and evaluating the controlled variable.
The final control element responds to the error signal by correcting the manipulated variable of the process.
the block diagram represents flowpaths of control signals, but does not represent flow of energy through the system or process.
The plant is the system or process through which a particular quantity or condition is controlled.
The control elements are components needed to generate the appropriate control signal applied to the plant.
The feedback elements are components needed to identify the functional relationship between the feedback signal and the controlled output.
The reference point is an external signal applied to the summing point of the control system to cause the plant to produce a specified action.
The actuating signal represents the control action of the control loop and is equal to the algebraic sum of the reference input signal and feedback signal.
The disturbance is an undesirable input signal that upsets the value of the controlled output of the plant.
The lube oil temperature is the controlled variable because it is maintained at a desired value (the setpoint).
Cooling water flow rate is the manipulated variable because it is adjusted by the temperature control valve to maintain the lube oil temperature.
Process time lags are caused by three properties of the process.
Capacitance is the ability of a process to store energy.
Resistance is that part of the process that opposes the transfer of energy between capacities.
Transportation time is time required to carry a change in a process variable from one point to another in the process.
it is an actual time delay during which no change occurs.
Stability is the ability of a control loop to return a controlled variable to a steady, non-cyclic value, following a disturbance.
This is the condition desired in an automatic control system.
A two position controller is a device that has two operating conditions: completely on or completely off.
This opening and closing of the final control element results in a cycling characteristic of the measured variable.
Deviation is the difference between the setpoint of a process variable and its actual value.
In other words, amount of valve movement is proportional to amount of deviation.
Proportional band, (also called throttling range), is the change in value of the controlled variable that causes full travel of the final control element.
Mathematically, gain and sensitivity are reciprocal to proportional band.
Offset, also called droop, is deviation that remains after a process has stabilized.
Bistables are two-position switches that are either on or off, depending on the input variable.

passages.quote: Proportional band is the change in input required to produce a full range of change in the output due to the proportional control action.
The proportional controller is reverse-acting so that the control valve throttles down to reduce steam flow as the hot water outlet temperature increases
Direct acting controllers or actuators will respond in the same direction as the control signal

passages.quote: Integral control describes a controller in which the output rate of change is dependent on the magnitude of the input.
The major advantage of integral controllers is that they have the unique ability to return the controlled variable back to the exact setpoint following a disturbance.
the integral control mode is not normally used alone, but is combined with another control mode.
Output rate of change = Integral constant x % Error
It combines the immediate output characteristics of a proportional control mode with the zero residual offset characteristics of the integral mode.
a large sustained error signal will eventually cause the controller to drive to its limit, and the result is called "reset windup."
this control mode is not well-suited for processes that are frequently shut down and started up.
This derivative section responds to the rate of change of the error signal, not the amplitude
Derivative cannot be used alone as a control mode.
This is because a steady-state input produces a zero output in a differentiator.
Thus, derivative action provides increased stability to the system, but does not eliminate offset error.
Proportional plus rate control is normally used with large capacity or slow-responding processes such as temperature control.
Rate action is not usually employed with fast responding processes such as flow control or noisy processes
there are some processes that cannot tolerate offset error, yet need good stability.
The PID controller combines the three individual modes to achieve the advantages of each.
The rate action combined with the proportional action reduces the initial overshoot and cyclic period.
Control stations perform the function of a controller and provide additional controls and indicators to allow an operator to manually adjust the controller output to the final control element.
The setpoint indicator displays the desired value for the controller.
The dial adjustment used to vary the setpoint value is the setpoint adjustment.
The deviation indicator displays the difference in percentages between the setpoint value and the actual controlled variable value.
Percentage display for the output signal is indicated on the output meter.
The manual-automatic transfer switch is a five position switch that alters the mode of operation.
Located in the center of the transfer switch, the manual output adjustment knob varies the controller output signal in the manual mode of operation.
Bumpless transfer is the smooth transfer of a controller from one operating mode to another.
Self-balancing describes a control station in which the non-operating mode output signal follows (tracks) the operating mode output signal.
Final control elements are devices that complete the control loop.
Of the final control elements discussed, the most widely used in power plants are valves.
These devices are called actuators.
A positioner is a device that regulates the supply air pressure to a pneumatic actuator.
On a loss of supply air, the actuator in Figure 36 will fail open.
This "fail-safe" concept is an important consideration in nuclear facility design.
when a large amount of force is required to operate a valve
First, they have only two positions: fully open and fully closed. Second, they don’t produce much force, so they usually only operate relatively small valves.
A major advantage of solenoid actuators is their quick operation.
Limit switches de-energize the electric motor when the valve has reached a specific position.
The clutch and clutch lever disconnects the electric motor from the gear assembly and allows the valve to be operated manually with the handwheel.

body.text: If a control system fails, the operator must be able to take over and control the process manually.

checks.q: What defines an open-loop control system?
o: Control action is independent of the output
Control action depends on the output
checks.x: An open-loop control system is one in which the control action is independent of the output.

checks.q: In a tank level control system, what is the flow rate of supply water?
checks.x: The flow rate of the water supplied to the tank is the manipulated variable.

checks.q: In a tank level control system, what is the tank level?
checks.x: The level is maintained at a specified value, so it is the controlled variable.

body.text: Three elements perform these functions: a measurement element, an error detection element, and a final control element.

body.cap: Relationships of Functions and Elements in an Automatic Control System
body.alt: Relationship of measurement, error detection, and final control elements around a process.

body.text: The error detection element compares the controlled variable to the desired value and signals an error if there is a deviation.

checks.q: What are the four basic functions in any automatic control system?
checks.x: The four basic functions are measurement, comparison, computation, and correction.

body.text: A block diagram shows the cause and effect relationship between the input and output of a physical system. Arrows show signal flow.
A summing point shows addition and subtraction. A takeoff point allows a signal to be used by more than one block or summing point.

body.alt: Feedback control block diagram: reference input to a summing point, control elements, the plant, controlled output, and feedback elements, with a disturbance input.

body.text: The reference point is also called the setpoint.
The feedback signal is a function of the output signal.
The actuating signal is also called the error signal.

checks.q: What is another name for the actuating signal?
checks.x: The actuating signal is also called the error signal.

checks.q: What is another name for the reference point?
checks.x: The reference point represents the desired value and is also called the setpoint.

checks.q: What does a control system block diagram represent?
o: Flow of energy through the process
checks.x: The block diagram represents flowpaths of control signals, not the flow of energy.

checks.q: What is a disturbance?
o: An undesirable input signal that upsets the controlled output
checks.x: The disturbance is an undesirable input signal that upsets the value of the controlled output.

body.cap: Lube Oil Cooler Temperature Control System and Equivalent Block Diagram
body.alt: Lube oil cooler with a temperature transmitter, temperature controller, and cooling water valve, and the equivalent block diagram.

body.text: Cooling water flows in the shell around tubes that carry lube oil.
If the temperature is above the setpoint, the controller moves the valve in the open direction, which sends more cooling water through the cooler.
The lube oil cooler is the plant, and the temperature transmitter is the feedback element.
The actuating signal passes through the temperature controller and the control valve.

checks.q: In the lube oil cooler loop, what is the manipulated variable?
checks.x: Cooling water flow rate is the manipulated variable, adjusted by the temperature control valve.

body.text: Instability is caused by a combination of process time lags and time lags within the control system.

body.alt: Three plots of the controlled variable: decreasing, constant, and increasing amplitude oscillations.

body.text: Decreasing amplitude oscillations eventually stop.
Constant amplitude never reaches a stable condition. Increasing amplitude causes the process to go out of control.

checks.q: Which three properties cause process time lags?
checks.x: Process time lags are caused by capacitance, resistance, and transportation time.

checks.q: What is capacitance in a process?
o: The ability of a process to store energy
checks.x: Capacitance is the ability of a process to store energy.

checks.q: How does transportation time differ from a slowing of change?
o: It is an actual time delay during which no change occurs
It only occurs in heat exchangers
checks.x: This lag is an actual time delay during which no change occurs.

checks.q: Which type of oscillation is desired in an automatic control system?
checks.x: Decreasing amplitude is the condition desired in an automatic control system.

body.text: The output is determined by whether the error signal is above or below the setpoint.

checks.q: What characteristic does a two position controller give the measured variable?
checks.x: The opening and closing of the final control element results in a cycling characteristic of the measured variable.

body.text: The proportional mode responds only to the amount of deviation and is insensitive to rate or duration.
Offset is an inherent characteristic of the proportional mode.

checks.q: How are gain and proportional band related?
o: Gain is the square of proportional band
checks.x: Gain and sensitivity are reciprocal to proportional band.

checks.q: What is offset?
o: The change that causes full valve travel
The rate of change of the error
Deviation that remains after a process has stabilized
checks.x: Offset, also called droop, is deviation that remains after a process has stabilized.

checks.q: An instrument has a full range of 200 °F and a 50 °F change causes full valve travel. What is the proportional band?

body.text: A smaller input causes a slower rate of change of the output. It is also known as reset control.

body.cap: Integral Output for a Fixed Input
body.alt: Integrator input step and the output ramp that rises at a constant rate.

body.text: A large error moves the final control element rapidly, and a small error moves it slowly.
Disadvantages are a relatively slow response and a possibly large initial deviation.

checks.q: What is the major advantage of integral control?
o: It returns the controlled variable to the exact setpoint
checks.x: Integral controllers can return the controlled variable back to the exact setpoint following a disturbance.

checks.q: An integral controller has a constant of 0.1 per second and a 5% error. What is its output rate of change?
checks.x: Output rate of change = integral constant x % error = 0.1 x 5 = 0.5% per second.

body.text: Proportional action gives an immediate output but leaves a residual offset. Integral action keeps repositioning the final control element until the error is reduced to zero.

body.cap: Response of Proportional Plus Reset Control
body.alt: Plots of an error signal and the proportional plus reset controller output, with a step followed by a ramp.

body.text: Reset action also makes the process return to setpoint more quickly.

checks.q: What is reset windup?
o: A large sustained error drives the controller to its limit
A bump on transfer to manual
checks.x: A large sustained error signal eventually drives the controller to its limit, which is called reset windup.

checks.q: What does adding reset to proportional control eliminate?
o: All deviation at the instant of a change
checks.x: Proportional plus reset combines the immediate output with zero residual offset.

body.text: Derivative action reduces initial overshoot and helps stabilize the process sooner.

body.cap: Response of Proportional Plus Rate Control
body.alt: Plots of an error signal and the proportional plus rate controller output.

body.text: It is useful for processes frequently started up and shut down, because it is not susceptible to reset windup.

checks.q: Why is rate action not usually used on flow control?
o: It responds to any rate of change, including noise
checks.x: Derivative action responds to any rate of change in the error signal, including the noise.

body.text: Two position control suits processes that can operate with continuous cycling. Proportional control suits those that cannot.

body.alt: Curves of the proportional, reset, and rate actions and their combined output for a slowly increasing error.

items: The proportional action responds to the error amplitude
The integral action eliminates the offset error
The derivative action provides additional stability to the process

checks.q: In a PID controller, which action eliminates offset error?
checks.x: The integral action eliminates the offset error.

body.alt: Front panel of a control station with setpoint and deviation indicators, an output meter, and a manual-automatic switch.

body.text: The five positions are AUTO, 0-100 on the auto side, MAN, 0-100 on the manual side, and BAL.
Without a match, the final control element could get a sudden change, or bump, causing large swings in the process variable.

checks.q: What does the deviation indicator on a control station show?
o: The difference between setpoint and the controlled variable
checks.x: The deviation indicator displays the difference between the setpoint value and the actual controlled variable value.

checks.q: What does the manual output adjust knob do?
o: Varies controller output in manual mode
checks.x: The manual output adjustment knob varies the controller output signal in the manual mode of operation.

concepts.title: Self-balancing stations and final control elements

body.alt: Self-balancing control station with manual push buttons, mode lights, and mode selection buttons.

body.text: This station does not need a balancing procedure before shifting modes.
After transfer to manual, the output stays at its previous value until a manual push button is pressed.
After transfer to automatic, any deviation is removed slowly.
Manual push buttons have half-in and full-in positions. At full-in, the output changes about ten times faster.
Other final control elements include dampers, pumps, and electric heaters.

checks.q: What does self-balancing mean on a control station?
o: The non-operating mode output tracks the operating mode output
checks.x: In a self-balancing station, the non-operating mode output signal follows the operating mode output signal.

body.text: Valves that must be operated remotely and automatically need special devices to move them.

body.alt: Pneumatic actuator: supply air above a rubber diaphragm, a spring below, and a stem to the control valve.

body.text: A pneumatic actuator operates by a combination of force created by air and spring force.
With no supply air, the spring holds the valve fully open. Increasing air pressure closes the valve.

body.cap: Pneumatic Actuator with Controller and Positioner
body.alt: Pneumatic actuator with a controller and a positioner connected by a feedback linkage.

body.text: A positioner compares the demanded position with the actual position.
This is called air-to-close, spring-to-open, or fail-open. Others are air-to-open, spring-to-close, or fail-closed.

checks.q: An air-to-close, spring-to-open actuator loses supply air. What does the valve do?
checks.x: On a loss of supply air, the spring moves the actuator and the valve fails open.

body.text: Hydraulic actuators are normally used

body.alt: Piston-type hydraulic actuator with a spring above the piston and hydraulic oil below.

body.text: Hydraulic pressure on the piston overcomes the spring and opens the valve. Draining oil lets the spring close it.

body.alt: Solenoid actuator with a coil, an armature, a spring, and a stem.

body.text: Current through a solenoid coil forms a magnetic field that attracts the armature and opens the valve. When current stops, the spring shuts the valve.

body.alt: Electric motor actuator with a motor, a clutch and gear box assembly, a handwheel, and a stem.

body.text: The motor reverses its rotation to open or close the valve.
Torque limiters de-energize the motor when turning force reaches a specified value.

checks.q: When are hydraulic actuators normally used?
o: When a very small valve is used
When quick response only is needed
When a large amount of force is required
checks.x: When a large amount of force is required to operate a valve, hydraulic actuators are normally used.

checks.q: What are the two disadvantages of solenoid actuators?
o: Only two positions, and not much force
checks.x: Solenoid actuators have only two positions and don't produce much force.

checks.q: How is an electric motor actuated valve operated by hand?
o: The limit switch is held closed
A clutch disconnects the motor so the handwheel can be used
checks.x: The clutch and lever disconnect the motor from the gear assembly, allowing use of the handwheel.

facts.q: What are the three functional elements of an automatic control system?
facts.a: A measurement element, an error detection element, and a final control element.
The control action of the loop, equal to the algebraic sum of the reference input and feedback signals. It is also called the error signal.
The change in the controlled variable that causes full travel of the final control element.

facts.q: Why can't derivative control be used alone?
facts.a: A steady-state input produces a zero output in a differentiator.

facts.q: What does each PID action do?
facts.a: Proportional responds to error amplitude, integral eliminates offset, and derivative adds stability.
It regulates the supply air pressure to a pneumatic actuator by comparing demanded position with actual position.

facts.q: What does fail-open mean on a pneumatic actuator?

summary.text: A control system maintains a process variable at a desired value or within a desired range.
Process time lags are affected by capacitance, resistance, and transportation time.
A two position controller has two operating conditions: completely on or completely off.
Proportional plus reset control eliminates any offset error that would occur with proportional control only.
Proportional plus rate control increases system stability but does not eliminate offset error.
The PID controller combines the three individual modes to achieve the advantages of each.
Actuators may be pneumatic, hydraulic, solenoid, or electric motor types.
